title: St Paul's Cathedral
blurb: Sir Christopher Wren’s English Baroque cathedral on Ludgate Hill, built 1675 to 1710 after the Great Fire of London. Explore the 158 m plan, the twin 67 m west towers, and the triple dome rising to 111 m on eight great piers.

sourceUrls.label: Project Gutenberg: Views of St. Paul’s Cathedral
ATC UK: Wren, St Paul’s Cathedral study sheet

systems.name: Base and podium
systems.description: The podium, west steps and crypt plinth the cathedral stands on.

systems.name: West front
systems.description: The 55 m wide west front: two storeys in Corinthian and Composite orders with a pediment, portico, doors and statues.

systems.name: West towers
systems.description: The twin 67 m west towers with clock stages, belfries, bell-shaped cupolas and gilded pinecone finials.

systems.name: Nave
systems.description: The 37 m wide nave with its arcades, aisles, clerestory and barrel vault rising to 27 m.

systems.name: Transepts
systems.description: The north and south transept arms, 75 m across from end to end, with pedimented fronts and porticoes.

systems.name: Choir and apse
systems.description: The choir east of the crossing with its aisles, vault, semicircular apse and high altar platform.

systems.name: Dome
systems.description: Wren’s triple dome: inner dome, structural brick cone and timber-framed outer dome rising to 111 m, carried on eight great piers.

systems.name: Roofs
systems.description: The lead roofs over nave, aisles, choir and transepts.
